original_question: If C is a reduced supersolvable plane curve, meaning that C has at least one modular point p for which the projection from p induces a locally trivial fibration of the complement P^2 \ C, must C always be free?
target_in_paper: Section 8, Conjecture 8.2: Any supersolvable plane curve is free.
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct conjectural target: a reduced supersolvable plane curve, defined via the existence of a modular point whose central projection gives a locally trivial fibration of the complement, and asks exactly whether such a curve must be free. That is essentially the content of Conjecture 8.2.
missing_details: The ambient setting in the paper is the complex projective plane: C should be a reduced plane curve C = V(f) subset P^2_C, with f a reduced homogeneous polynomial in S = C[x,y,z].
In Definition 8.1, the modular point is required to satisfy p in C; your draft says there is a modular point p, but does not state explicitly that p lies on the curve.

For a stand-alone formulation, free should be defined in the plane-curve sense used earlier in the paper: D0(f) = {(a,b,c) in S^3 : a f_x + b f_y + c f_z = 0} is a free S-module of rank 2; equivalently, the curve is a 2-syzygy curve.

The paper's conjecture has no extra hypotheses such as quasi-homogeneity, degree bounds, or an adding-lines construction; those belong only to the supporting special case in Theorem 8.3 and should not be inserted into the main question.

If one wants the definition of modular point to be fully internalized, the paper gives an equivalent criterion: for every line L_p through p that is not an irreducible component of C, one has (C,L_p)_p = mult_p(C) and (C,L_p)_q = 1 for every q in C cap L_p with q != p.
refined_question: Let C = V(f) subset P^2_C be a reduced plane curve, where f is a reduced homogeneous polynomial in S = C[x,y,z]. Suppose there exists a point p in C such that the central projection pi_p: P^2_C \ {p} -> P^1_C restricts to a locally trivial fibration on the complement M(C) = P^2_C \ C; equivalently, suppose C is supersolvable in the sense of Definition 8.1. Must C be a free plane curve, i.e. must its Jacobian syzygy module D0(f) = {(a,b,c) in S^3 : a f_x + b f_y + c f_z = 0} be a free S-module of rank 2?
equivalent_formulation: Let C subset P^2_C be a reduced plane curve. If there exists p in C such that for every line L_p through p which is not an irreducible component of C one has (C,L_p)_p = mult_p(C) and (C,L_p)_q = 1 for every q in C cap L_p with q != p, does it follow that C is free?
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Conjecture 8.2 in Section 8, not a broader neighboring question. Definition 8.1 introduces modular points and supersolvable plane curves, and your draft tracks that definition closely. The only paper-faithful corrections needed are to specify that the ambient space is the complex projective plane, that the modular point satisfies p in C, and that freeness is meant in the earlier Section 2 sense for the Jacobian syzygy module D0(f). Theorem 8.3 is explicitly presented as a supporting special case where the conjecture is known, so it should be used for scope control and context, not as part of the conjecture's hypothesis.
